courses.title: History of Hong Kong
courses.faculty: Faculty of Health and Social Sciences
courses.objectives: This course focuses on the history of Hong Kong from 1841 to 1997, covering cultural, political, social, and economic issues. It aims to explain current circumstances through history while conveying the evolving nature of historical interpretation. Students will be encouraged to observe how interpretations of historical events stem from observers’ preconceptions and historical positions, and that historical facts acquire meaning only in relation to historical questions.
courses.summary: The course focuses on: the history of Hong Kong from 1841 to 1997, covering cultural, political, social, and economic issues. Teaching mode: primarily lecture-based, closely following assigned readings; students are required to complete pre-class reading.

This course focuses on the history of Hong Kong from 1842 to 1997, covering cultural, political, social, and economic issues. Rather than focusing solely on what happened in the past, the course teaches the following topics analytically and critically by presenting diverse perspectives drawn from multiple sources, thereby developing students’ relevant competencies.
Understand the opium trade during the early colonial period.
Understand the establishment of the colonial system.
